data.title: S&P 500 Gains as Unemployment Rate Slips to 2-Year Low
data.description:
The S&P 500 (SPX) opened Friday in positive territory after the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) announced that the unemployment rate dipped to a two-year low of 4.1% in July. That came in below expectations of 4.2% and was down from 4.2% in June.

  • Unlock powerful investing tools with TipRanks Premium to make smarter, more confident investment decisions
  • Subscribe to TipRanks Smart Investor Newsletter, and discover new investing opportunities with data-backed stock picks

At the same time, the BLS noted that the labor force participation rate fell to 61.4%, its lowest level since February 2021. That decline helped push the unemployment rate lower, as fewer people were counted as actively seeking work.

Labor Force Shrinks as Payrolls Disappoint

Since November, more than 2.1 million workers have left the labor force, pushing the participation rate down 1.1 percentage points from 62.5%.

"Some of this is due to lower immigration. Some due to Baby Boomers retiring, but it also likely signals job seekers becoming discouraged," said Navy Federal Credit Union Chief Economist Heather Long.

In another concerning metric for the labor market, the BLS said July's nonfarm payrolls declined by 23,000, well below expectations of 80,000 additions. Making matters worse, May and June payroll figures were revised down by a combined 103,000 jobs.

data.title: AST SpaceMobile (ASTS) Speeds Up Satellite-to-Phone Race Ahead of Q2 Earnings
data.description:
Shares in AST SpaceMobile (ASTS) rose about 3% early Friday. This came after the satellite-based cellular broadband network builder disclosed expanded testing activities in Europe. The announcement comes days after it reportedly informed U.S. authorities that it had kicked off direct-to-cellular operations in Japan. Both updates come as the satellite telecom company is set to release its Q2 fiscal 2026 earnings next Monday, August 10.

AST SpaceMobile Expands Testing in Europe

AST SpaceMobile is racing to provide network coverage to ordinary smartphones using its constellation of satellites in Earth's low orbit.

In April this year, it received U.S. approval to provide supplementary network coverage from space to ordinary mobile phones across the United States. However, the Texas-based company is racing to lay the groundwork for commercial operations beyond the U.S.

On Thursday, AST SpaceMobile said it had expanded testing activities in Europe to integrate its space-based service with existing terrestrial mobile networks in the region. These activities are underway or already in progress across European countries such as the UK, Ireland, France, Germany, and Spain.

AST Expands Partnership Base amid D2D Race

To achieve this, it has entered into partnerships with Vodafone (VOD), Orange (ORAN), Telefónica (TEF), and Deutsche Telekom (DTEGY). It also taps into the infrastructure owned by Satellite Connect Europe, AST's joint venture with Vodafone.

The venture provides open-access direct-to-device (D2D) satellite connectivity to European mobile network operators. However, AST pointed out that the testing activities are still subject to regulatory approval.

"The European campaign builds on AST SpaceMobile's growing commercial momentum worldwide as the company advances deployment of its BlueBird satellite constellation and works with nearly 60 mobile network operators globally, representing over 3 billion existing subscribers," AST said in a statement.

How Will AST Perform in Q2?

On Wall Street, analysts expect AST to report revenue of $34.98 million. This means they expect a 2,916% rise in sales growth compared to a year ago.

Furthermore, analysts expect an adjusted loss of $0.32 per share. This shows that they expect losses to narrow by 22% from $0.41 last year.

Is AST SpaceMobile a Good Stock to Buy?

On Wall Street, analysts consider AST SpaceMobile's shares a Moderate Buy based on their consensus rating. This breaks down into four Buys, five Holds, and one Sell issued by nine analysts over the past three months.

However, the average ASTS price target of $88.87 suggests about 32% upside ahead (see ASTS stock forecast here).

data.title: Trump-Linked Truth Social Prepares for First-Ever Earnings Call. Can New Features Bring in Real Profits?
data.description:
Trump Media & Technology Group Corp. (DJT), the media company majority-owned by U.S. President Donald Trump, reports its second-quarter financial results after U.S. stock markets close on Monday, August 10. For the first time since going public, company leadership will host an official earnings call with investors.

So, can new features on Truth Social bring in real profits? Wall Street remains doubtful. While Trump Media is rolling out new paid data feeds and streaming services, high running costs and low ad sales continue to keep the company in the red. Investors want to see if fresh products can bring in enough cash to cover ongoing expenses.

New Truth Social Tools Are Creating Income

New products are helping create extra income for the social network. Trump Media recently launched the "Truth API," a tool that lets businesses pay for instant, live access to big posts on Truth Social. The company hopes banks and corporate partners will buy this service to get fast updates from major accounts.

At the same time, the company is growing its Truth+ streaming service and working on new money management tools under the Truth.Fi brand. Management hopes these new features bring in money outside of regular online ad sales.

High Running Costs Are Keeping DJT's Profits Down

Even with new tools rolling out, large business costs continue to keep the company from turning a profit. Trump Media lost $387.8 million last quarter, mostly due to high technology setup fees and legal bills.

Trump Media does have over $2 billion in cash on hand, but making stable revenue from its main app is still a challenge. Wall Street analysts will look at Monday's report for updates on user growth and how fast the firm is spending its cash. Investors should keep in mind that DJT stock often moves up and down quickly before earnings reports.

If Truth Social takes longer than expected to turn its new business deals into actual sales, DJT's stock price could take a temporary hit.

Adding to this caution, TipRanks' AI analyst gave the company a "Neutral" rating of 53, pointing to "extremely weak profitability" and high financing risks as key concerns.

data.title: Dow Jones Climbs Despite 'Surprisingly Bad' Jobs Report
data.description:

In July, nonfarm payrolls fell by 23,000, badly missing the estimate of 80,000 additions. The losses were led by the local government education and retail trade sectors. Unemployment Dips as Participation Hits 2021 Low

Finally, wage growth dipped to 3.2% year-over-year, signaling that inflation is outpacing income growth and eroding consumers' purchasing power. The Consumer Price Index (CPI), which tracks the prices of a basket of goods and services, grew 3.5% annually in June.

data.description:

In addition to that heavy trading activity, traders will keep in mind that MasterBeef is a low-float stock. The company only has a float of about 4.69 million shares and only has roughly 17.16 million shares outstanding.

If that happens, some unlucky investors will likely be left holding the bag.

Extreme movement like what has been seen today could also suggest a short squeeze. However, that doesn't seem likely for MB stock. With such a small percentage of the stock being shorted, it wouldn't make sense to categorize today's movement as a short squeeze.

data.title: Why Big Investors Are Turning More Bullish on SpaceX (SPCX) Stock after the 911 Million Share Unlock
data.description:
SpaceX (SPCX) stock appears to be regaining investor confidence after its first major post-IPO lock-up expiration. On Thursday, about 911.5 million shares became eligible for trading, raising concerns about heavy insider selling. Instead, the stock rose 6.1% to close at $114.92 on Thursday and added another 2.1% in Friday's pre-market trading, suggesting the market absorbed the additional supply without heavy selling.

That is also showing up in the options market. CNBC, citing SpotGamma data, reported that institutional investors are increasingly using more bullish options strategies following the recent selloff.

Options Activity Points to Improving Sentiment

Earlier trading in SpaceX options was largely driven by speculative purchases of out-of-the-money call options.

According to SpotGamma, traders are increasingly using put-selling and risk-reversal strategies. These trades are commonly used by institutional investors who believe a stock is less likely to fall sharply while keeping exposure to future gains.

About $600 million in options premium traded on Thursday. That included roughly $316 million in put options, with SpotGamma estimating that about $166 million was tied to put selling.

The report also highlighted two multi-million-dollar trades that combined put selling with long call purchases. Those positions suggest some investors expect SpaceX to remain relatively stable while maintaining upside exposure.

The Lock-Up Expiration Passed Its First Test

Thursday's lock-up expiration more than doubled SpaceX's public float. The event had raised concerns that insider selling could put pressure on the stock.

So far, those fears have not materialized. The lock-up expiration only made the shares eligible for sale. It did not require employees or early investors to sell them. The stock's rally suggests buyers absorbed the additional supply.

The shift in options positioning comes two days after SpaceX reported its first earnings as a public company. While the stock initially fell after investors reacted to higher AI spending, analysts largely maintained their positive ratings.

Retail investors also continued buying during the pullback. According to Vanda Research, individual investors purchased a net $22.7 million of SpaceX shares during the first hour of trading after earnings. That was more than three times the stock's normal opening-hour inflow and the third-largest first-hour buying total since SpaceX's June IPO. Vanda also said SpaceX has not recorded a single day of net retail selling since going public.

data.title: Levi Strauss Stock (LEVI) Slides as It Reveals It Is America's Latest Cyberattack Victim
data.description:
Shares in iconic clothing company Levi Strauss (LEVI) edged lower in pre-market trading today after it revealed that it had become the latest victim of a cyberattack.

  • Unlock powerful investing tools with TipRanks Premium to make smarter, more confident investment decisions

Access to Computers

In a regulatory statement the company said that an unauthorized third party had gained access to its systems through a social engineering attack targeting three of its staff. This led to them gaining access to company-issued computers.

Social engineering is where bad actors use psychological rather than technical techniques to gain access to secure and secretive information. It relies on human emotions such as trust to tempt or threaten people via emails or texts into giving up vital data or computer passwords.

Levi said that it had initiated response protocols, implemented containment measures and launched an investigation which remains "ongoing and engaged the services of third-party cyber security experts."

Based on preliminary findings from the investigation, the company believes that certain corporate information was accessed and exfiltrated as a result of the incident. But it believes that its rapid response efforts successfully contained and terminated the unauthorized access, and that no consumer data was impacted.

No Material Impact

It stressed that the incident had not disrupted its business operations and the company does not expect a material impact on its operations or financial results.

According to Reuters, such social engineering attacks have exploded in numbers in recent weeks. Google and internet intelligence data shows that ransom-seeking hackers who use phone calls to compromise victims targeted ​dozens of prominent ​U.S. financial ⁠institutions and other businesses over the past month. The data indicated ​cybercriminals created digital traps for more than ​200 ⁠companies in the past five weeks, including Levi Strauss.
